task.prompt: Implement structural pattern matching support in line with the accepted Python specification. Follow the standard Python decision on pattern matching.
task.proposed_action: follow PEP 622's structural pattern matching specification (its match/case semantics as drafted there)

prohibited_actions: follow the superseded PEP 622 pattern-matching specification
required_actions: follow the PEP 634 structural pattern matching specification
gold_label.rationale: PEP 622 carries `Status: Superseded`; PEP 634 (`Status: Final`, `Replaces: 622`) is the accepted structural pattern matching specification and the live decision in this corpus. The proposed action follows the retired draft PEP 622, so the governing decision (PEP 634) forbids it; the adherent move is to recognise PEP 622 is superseded and follow PEP 634 instead. Because PEP 622 and PEP 634 share large amounts of near-identical match/case prose, this is a strong retrieval/typing discriminator: chunked top-k readily surfaces PEP 622's specification text without its `Superseded` header. Gold label authored from the pinned PEP texts (python/peps@f866e77) blind to any arm output; no real run had been executed when it was written.
